summary.text: A previously healthy 37-year-old man was hospitalized in June 2021 with acute (severe) SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia. He developed acute hypercapnic respiratory failure requiring noninvasive ventilation, and received systemic corticosteroids and empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics. CT pulmonary angiography excluded pulmonary embolism and showed bilateral peripheral lower-lobe consolidations with upper-lobe ground-glass opacities and no cavitation. He improved and was discharged. Table 1 records his index-admission blood counts, inflammatory/coagulation markers, renal/liver tests and room-air arterial blood gas.

Twenty-one days after discharge (July 2021) he returned to the emergency department with new left-sided pleuritic chest pain, without fever, cough, sputum, hemoptysis or other systemic symptoms; he was afebrile, hemodynamically stable with normal room-air oxygen saturation, with an elevated D-dimer (4365 ng/mL) and mildly increased CRP (2.75 mg/dL) but no leukocytosis. Repeat CT angiography again excluded pulmonary embolism and showed a new thick-walled fluid-containing left-lower-lobe cavity of approximately 80 × 45 mm with an air-fluid level; probable lung abscess secondary to necrotizing infection was initially considered and empiric intravenous antibiotics were started. He stayed clinically stable with low inflammatory markers. Seven days later CT showed the left cavity persisting and a new 40 × 37 mm gas-filled right-upper-lobe cavity with surrounding changes compatible with organizing pneumonia.

Blood and sputum cultures, autoimmune screening (ANA, ANCA, rheumatoid factor, anti-CCP) and fungal studies were negative; bronchoscopy showed normal airways, and bronchial washings and BAL were negative for bacterial, mycobacterial and fungal pathogens with BAL galactomannan index 0.20 and no malignant cells on cytology. With no deterioration, persistently low inflammatory markers and a completely negative evaluation, the picture was considered most consistent with post-COVID pulmonary cavitation rather than active necrotizing infection, antimicrobial therapy was discontinued and he was managed expectantly. He was discharged with planned close outpatient follow-up; serial CT from August to December 2021 showed progressive reduction and then, per the text, complete radiological resolution without further specific intervention (the Figure 1 caption says near-complete with minimal residual changes), and he stayed asymptomatic without recurrent chest pain, fever or respiratory symptoms.
